notes.148v.1: Ivie riffe is kept as a word of power; 'hin vile michel' is taken as 'away, very great one', but may itself be a formula. veimen (148v.5) is 'skim off'; its sense here is uncertain. 'daz uns ze lüppe' (148v.6) is obscure (lüppe is 'poison, witchcraft') and seems incomplete; it may also mean 'may this serve us as a charm'. 'ûf harte' may be 'on the wooded hill'; 'engelen dû jagetes' (you hunted angels) is odd; the negative in '[no] more' is supplied. Pat̄ and Pater are taken as the Our Father; 'Mm.' is unexplained.

nodes.text: Ivie riffe. Ivie riffe. Ivie riffe. Away, very great one! Away, very great one!
Away, very great one! Where do black clouds come from?
That is the holy Christ with his splendour; that is the holy
Christ with his host. He parts the dark clouds;
he will skim off the white stones, so that they melt before they come to earth,
before these same holy words. That [came] to us by witchcraft. Our Father. Our Father.
Our Father. Do you remember now, hail, where the watchmen saw you in the
clouds? On the hard [ground] you lay; you hunted angels; so that you dare [no] more,
wherever you are named. Mm. Our Father.
